skill.name: dead-code-removal
skill.description: Detects unused imports, functions, and classes across several languages, then guides conservative removal with backups and validation checks.
skill.summary: Finds likely dead code and guides incremental cleanup with validation.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown formatting false positives, including inline file names, examples, and safety notes about dynamic language features. Real residual risks remain where the skill documents shell-based backups and validation commands that can copy sensitive files or execute project-defined test scripts.

remediation.issue: Backup command recursively copies the entire workspace into a local directory.
remediation.suggestion: Create backups outside the repository or use a VCS-based diff workflow. Exclude secrets, dependency directories, generated files, and existing backups.

remediation.issue: Validation examples run project-defined commands such as npm test, pytest, npx eslint, and mvn test.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running project commands, especially in untrusted repositories. Show the exact command before execution.

remediation.issue: The cleanup workflow can modify source files while removing dead code.
remediation.suggestion: Always present a proposed diff, apply small batches, and stop when dynamic usage or public API uncertainty exists.

content.value_statement: Unused imports and abandoned functions add noise, maintenance cost, and bundle weight. This skill finds likely dead code, removes safe items incrementally, and validates changes.
actual_capabilities: Detects common project languages, entry points, and critical source files.
Uses an AST-based helper script to identify unused Python imports.
Checks imports, calls, inheritance, exports, and framework preservation patterns.
Creates backups before edits and removes code in small validated steps.
Runs syntax, test, lint, or build checks when matching project tools exist.
limitations: Dynamic references, reflection, plugins, templates, and generated code can hide real usage.
The included helper script only analyzes Python imports, not functions or classes.
Validation depends on project tools, installed dependencies, and reliable test coverage.
The skill can edit files, so users should review diffs before accepting removals.

use_cases.title: Prepare A Refactored Feature Branch
use_cases.description: Find leftover imports and private helpers after a feature rewrite, then remove only clearly unused items.

use_cases.title: Reduce Frontend Bundle Noise
use_cases.description: Review JavaScript or TypeScript modules for abandoned utilities while preserving exports, routes, and framework components.

use_cases.title: Audit Legacy Services
use_cases.description: Map old service code, identify unused functions, and report preserved items that need human review.

prompt_templates.title: Find Unused Imports
prompt_templates.prompt: Find unused imports in the files I specify. Report what looks safe to remove and wait before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Clean One Directory Conservatively
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the src directory for dead code. Preserve exports, framework hooks, tests, and dynamic references. Remove only low-risk items.

prompt_templates.title: Validate After Refactoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this refactored branch for unused imports, functions, and classes. Create a removal plan, apply small changes, and run available validation.

prompt_templates.title: Audit A Mixed Codebase
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this mixed-language repository for dead code. Map entry points, preserve public APIs, flag uncertain findings, and summarize every kept risk.

output_examples.input: Clean up unused imports in a Python utility file.
output_examples.output: A concise report lists total imports, unused candidates, preserved dynamic references, removed lines, and validation status.

output_examples.input: Find unused functions in a service directory.
output_examples.output: A directory summary names each candidate, explains the reference search, removes one safe private helper, and preserves one routed function.

output_examples.input: Review dead code before a production release.
output_examples.output: A release cleanup summary shows files analyzed, changes made, tests run, unresolved risks, and recommended manual checks.

best_practices: Run the skill on a clean branch and inspect diffs after each removal.
Use conservative mode when dynamic access, reflection, or framework registration is present.
Run tests, lint checks, and builds after each small batch of changes.
anti_patterns: Removing public APIs because no internal references are found.
Deleting code across many directories without incremental validation.
Ignoring framework registrations, migrations, templates, generated code, or configuration.

faq.question: Can this skill delete files automatically?
faq.answer: It can edit project files during cleanup. Review the proposed diff before accepting any removal.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: It describes checks for Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, Go, and Rust project structures.

faq.question: Does the helper script analyze every language?
faq.answer: No. The included helper script uses Python AST parsing for unused Python imports only.

faq.question: How does it avoid deleting used code?
faq.answer: It preserves entry points, framework patterns, tests, exported APIs, and code with dynamic usage signals.

faq.question: Should I run tests afterward?
faq.answer: Yes. Run project tests and builds after each small cleanup batch.

faq.question: Is it suitable for large legacy repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, but use staged analysis and require manual review for uncertain functions or public interfaces.
